name: Lam Research Corporation

profile.description: Lam Research designs, manufactures, and services semiconductor processing equipment used in the fabrication of integrated circuits, holding dominant global market share in conductor etch (~50%) and leadership in deposition and clean technologies. FY2026 (ending June 2026) delivered record revenue of $23.23B (+26% YoY) with record EPS and gross margins expanding to 52%. The September 2026 quarter (FQ1 2027) produced $8.22B revenue with 52.3% gross margin and 40% operating margin, beating estimates. CEO Tim Archer projects the WFE market reaching the low $150B range driven by AI semiconductor investment.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Lam delivered record FY2026 revenue of $23.23B (+26% YoY) followed by a September quarter of $8.22B (beating estimates of $8.14B), driven by critical process solutions for AI-era semiconductors — high-bandwidth memory (HBM) etch and deposition, gate-all-around (GAA) transistor patterning, and advanced packaging [1]. Customer Support Business Group reached a record nearly $2.5B in the June quarter (+43% YoY), demonstrating successful installed-base monetization. AI Deployment (1/2): Lam is embedding AI sensors into chipmaking tools to identify process issues that were previously undetectable — CEO Archer said 'What AI is allowing us to do is identify conditions in the system that we didn't know were a problem before' — but AI is used for internal optimization rather than as a customer-facing product feature [2]. Market Share (2/2): Dominant global market share in conductor etch (~50%) and leadership in deposition — critical steps that increase in count with every technology node shrink, positioning Lam to outgrow the broader WFE market as AI chip complexity rises [1]. Pipeline (1/2): WFE spending forecast raised to low $150B range with management describing FY2027 as 'extraordinary,' and long-term margin targets of mid-50s% gross and mid-40s% operating provide a clear trajectory, though specific product launches are not publicly disclosed [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D spending of approximately $2.2B annually (~9.5% of revenue) exceeds the capital equipment industry average, sustaining leadership across etch and deposition for sub-2nm logic nodes.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): 'Creating a Better World Through Semiconductor Innovation' is a functional articulation connecting Lam's work to technological progress, but does not differentiate meaningfully from peer companies in the semiconductor equipment space and reads more as a business description than a transformative vision [2]. Community Impact (2/2): First U.S.-based semiconductor equipment maker with SBTi-approved near-term emissions targets, net zero by 2050 commitment, 20.1M gallons of water saved globally in 2023, 100% of top-tier suppliers engaged on sustainability, and named one of Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Tim Archer has served as CEO since 2018 with stable tenure, the February 2026 restructuring elevated existing leader Sesha Varadarajan to COO (promote-from-within culture), and headcount grew from 20,600 to 22,400 in FY2026, but no specific turnover or engagement metrics are available. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying; recent transactions include director stock sales.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock. Lam demonstrates exceptional financial strength across nearly every dimension [1]. D/E of 33.1% is well below the 70% target (score 1.0). ROE of 65.1% far exceeds the 15% target (score 1.0). Revenue growth YoY of 30% scores 1.0; 5-year revenue CAGR of approximately 10% (FY2021 $14.6B to FY2026 $23.2B) scores 1.0. Profit margin of 31.3% exceeds the 20% target (score 1.0). Forward P/E of 21.56 scores 0.96 — dramatically improved from the prior screen's 36.55x due to the stock's pullback from $315 to $261 alongside accelerating earnings [1]. Dividend metrics are uniformly strong: payout ratio of 20% (score 1.0), 12 consecutive years of payments (score 1.0, 2x weight), 12 consecutive years of growth (score 1.0), and 5-year dividend growth CAGR of 15% (score 1.0, 2x weight). Weighted sum 11.96/12 yields infrastructure score of 10. Liquidity is exceptional at ~$2.4B daily dollar volume.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Lam Research is semiconductor infrastructure — AI cannot exist without the equipment Lam builds [1]. Every advanced AI chip from NVIDIA, AMD, and custom silicon (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia) requires Lam's etch and deposition tools. AI directly increases demand: HBM production requires 3-4x more etch and deposition steps than conventional DRAM, advanced logic nodes demand more patterning layers, and WFE spending has been raised to $150B+ driven primarily by AI investment [2]. Lam's business involves physical manufacturing equipment with decade-long customer qualification cycles, creating near-zero substitution risk from AI. The sole risk is cyclical: if AI monetization disappoints and WFE spending corrects, the same AI tailwind becomes a headwind — but this is cyclical, not structural disruption. AI Opportunity (1/1): September 2026 quarter revenue of $8.22B (implying a $33B+ annual run rate versus FY2026's $23.2B) is directly attributable to AI-driven semiconductor investment, and management described FY2027 as 'extraordinary' due to AI demand [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Lam Research operates with the engineering discipline and long-term investment orientation characteristic of semiconductor capital equipment leaders — maintaining technology leadership through sustained R&D investment through downcycles while building a multi-product platform across etch, deposition, clean, and advanced packaging. However, the company's purpose is functional rather than transcendent, and strategic language emphasizes 'velocity in the AI era' and competitive outperformance rather than a deeply held cause that survives leadership transitions and market cycles.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Creating a Better World Through Semiconductor Innovation' provides genuine directional purpose — Lam's equipment enables virtually all advanced computing and AI technology — but the framing is interchangeable with peers and lacks the distinctive, never-fully-achievable quality of a true Just Cause [2]. Management references to the AI boom frame the company in commercial and competitive terms rather than purpose-driven sacrifice.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Lam has demonstrated stable leadership with Tim Archer serving as CEO since 2018 and the February 2026 restructuring elevating existing leader Varadarajan to COO rather than disrupting the organization [2]. Ethisphere's Most Ethical Companies recognition and headcount growth from 20,600 to 22,400 suggest a functional trust environment, but no specific employee empowerment, engagement, or retention metrics are publicly available.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Lam competes with Applied Materials (AMAT) and Tokyo Electron (TEL) in a market where technology leadership determines customer adoption, and management language focuses on 'outperforming the WFE market' and winning through technology transitions rather than destroying competitors [1]. The decision to reorganize leadership for faster innovation reflects a self-improvement orientation, though public acknowledgment of specific lessons from competitors is limited.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Lam has expanded from its core etch franchise into deposition, clean, and advanced packaging technologies over two decades, successfully diversifying its revenue base [1]. The strategic pivot to support AI-era semiconductor manufacturing — HBM, GAA transistors, backside power delivery — represents meaningful adaptation to new technology paradigms. Customer Support Business Group growing to record $2.5B quarterly revenue (+43% YoY) shows successful transformation of the installed-base business model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Lam maintained elevated R&D spending (~$2.2B annually) through the FY2023-2024 semiconductor equipment downturn when revenue declined from $17.4B to $14.9B, positioning the company for the AI recovery [1]. The company is adding headcount and inventory during the current boom, accepting higher cost risk if growth slows. These decisions reflect sound long-term thinking, though they are standard practices in the capital equipment industry.

investment_thesis: Lam Research at $260.81 (21.56x forward earnings) is a premium semiconductor equipment compounder riding the largest WFE investment cycle in history — FY2026 delivered record revenue of $23.23B (+26% YoY) with record 52% gross margins, followed by a September quarter of $8.22B that beat estimates and implies a $33B+ annual run rate, a dramatic step-change from the current fiscal year [1]. The AI buildout is structurally expanding Lam's addressable market: HBM requires 3-4x more etch/deposition steps, GAA transistors increase process complexity, and advanced packaging adds entirely new equipment layers. D/E of 33% with low leverage provides balance sheet optionality, while the 20% payout ratio and 15% 5-year dividend growth CAGR ensure reliable income compounding. The stock's 17% pullback from $315 to $261 has compressed the forward P/E from 36.6x to 21.6x, dramatically improving the risk-reward as earnings catch up to the lower price [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on cyclicality and concentration risk. The semiconductor equipment industry is inherently cyclical, and the current AI investment boom may prove front-loaded, with customer capacity additions outpacing end-market demand — WFE spending has historically experienced 20-30% peak-to-trough declines [1]. The 17% stock decline from $315 may reflect early signs of investor concern about sustainability of the AI capex cycle. U.S.-China export restrictions limit Lam's access to Chinese customers (historically 25-30% of industry revenue), and further tightening could accelerate Chinese domestic equipment development from NAURA and AMEC [3]. The Inspiration score of 5 reflects a company that excels at engineering execution but lacks the purpose-driven leadership IOWN values alongside financial performance. The Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED) limits allocation for faith-based investors despite strong positive attributions across 15 ESG categories.
key_catalysts: September 2026 quarter revenue of $8.22B (beating estimates of $8.14B) implies a $33B+ annual run rate versus FY2026's $23.2B, with WFE spending outlook raised to low $150B range and management describing FY2027 as 'extraordinary' [1][2]

Long-term margin expansion toward mid-50s% gross and mid-40s% operating margins as product mix shifts to higher-value AI-related process equipment, up from current 52.3% gross and 40% operating in the September quarter [1]

Stock pullback from $315 to $261 has compressed forward P/E from 36.6x to 21.6x, creating an improved entry point for a franchise delivering 30% revenue growth with record margins and dominant market share in etch and deposition [1]
key_risks: Semiconductor equipment cyclicality — WFE spending has historically experienced 20-30% peak-to-trough declines, and the current AI boom may front-load demand, creating correction risk if AI monetization fails to justify data center capex by 2028 [1]

U.S.-China export restriction escalation could further limit access to Chinese semiconductor manufacturers (historically 25-30% of industry revenue) while accelerating Chinese domestic equipment development from NAURA and AMEC [3]

Lam is adding headcount (20.6K to 22.4K) and inventory during the boom cycle, raising operating cost risk if WFE spending decelerates — the FY2023-2024 downturn saw revenue decline 14%, and a repeat could compress margins and earnings [1][2]

backlog.note: Lam does not disclose traditional order backlog; deferred revenue of $2.43B (+$213M sequentially) is used as funded backlog proxy. Semi equipment visibility comes from WFE market forecasts and customer fab investment announcements rather than traditional backlog. With WFE spending raised to low $150B and revenue running at $33B+ annual pace, underlying demand momentum is strong. Customer Support Business Group revenue of nearly $2.5B (+43% YoY) reflects expanding installed-base commitment.
